**Southwest has a dramatically stronger balance sheet** — it carries positive equity of $10.35B (vs. American's stockholders' deficit of nearly $4B, a legacy of American's post-bankruptcy/merger capital structure and heavy debt load from fleet financing and pandemic-era borrowing) and less than a third of American's long-term debt ($6.7B vs. $24.6B).

### Note on comparability
Both firms report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan–Dec 2024) using US GAAP, so the periods and accounting bases are directly comparable — no divestiture, spinoff, or fiscal-year mismatch adjustments are needed. **No.** American Airlines leads on (a) operating margin, while Southwest Airlines leads decisively on (b) balance-sheet strength (positive equity and much lower long-term debt).

Different airlines lead the two dimensions.
